properties.name: Massachusetts
properties.summary: On the cold shores of the northern Atlantic, Massachusetts binds proud free cities, inland lordships and ancient bishoprics beneath the white blossom of its banner. From the quays of Middlesex to the halls of Worcester, merchants and nobles bargain over the price of liberty. United against the Anglo-Saxon crown, they provision the rebellion even as old rivalries trouble the kingdom within.

properties.name: Mayan States
properties.summary: The Mayan States are a confederation of city-kingdoms across the Yucatan, the Peten and the Guatemalan highlands, tracing an unbroken line back to the true Maya civilization that first rose here in the Preclassic era, two thousand years before the Revolution. In this timeline, contact with Roman expeditions along the Gulf coast introduced iron tools, arch-and-vault masonry and the wheel to Maya engineers, technologies grafted onto an already sophisticated tradition of astronomy, hieroglyphic writing and monumental architecture. The States are less a single crown than a council of allied dynasties bound by shared script, calendar and cult. Their merchant fleets ply the Caribbean in strength, trading cacao, jade, cotton and Roman-taught glasswork for the apples, wine and coin of the Sidennic League, making the Sidennic-Mayan sea route one of the richest in the New World.
properties.boundaryStatus: Expanded to absorb neighbouring unclaimed provisional territory on 2026-09-11

properties.name: Aztec Empire
properties.summary: The Aztec Empire is the youngest great power of the New World, its capital Tenochtitlan raised barely two generations ago upon a lake in the Valley of Mexico, exactly as in our own history. Bound by tribute and marriage into the Triple Alliance with Texcoco and Tlacopan, its warrior-priests hold that the sun itself, Huitzilopochtli, must be fed with blood to rise each dawn -- the solar cult the golden rays of their banner proclaim. Chinampa farms feed a capital already among the largest cities in the world, while obsidian, cacao and featherwork move along tribute roads reaching from the Gulf to the Pacific. Wary of the Roman colonies and Mayan States to their east, the Aztecs have so far kept the newcomers' iron and glass at arm's length, trading only at the frontier and trusting more in their own gods and armies than in foreign wonders.
